about: In-scope rule for every binary group. scripts/gen-scope.py turns this file into the binaries and scope sections of scripts/inventory-config.json; docs/inventory/scope.tsv reports it. 'in' puts every function of the group in scope, 'narrow' only the functions whose names start with a prefix of narrow_prefixes, 'out' none. Out of scope means not yet: the inventory keeps listing the rows.

groups.reason: The linked kernels. Only the hardware-facing and boot-critical subsystems are in scope for now: PROM interface and KLCONFIG, hardware graph, interrupts, NUMA and memory initialisation, node and router topology, the I/O attach framework, and the debug and panic entry points.
Platform core and debugger objects hold both hardware-facing code and generic code, so the name rule of the kernel image applies to them as well.
Objects that exist only for the NUMA, hardware-graph, crossbar, bridge, node-board and attach machinery of the in-scope subsystems.

Every other kernel object (file systems, networking, STREAMS, NFS and RPC, CXFS stubs, scheduler and virtual memory in os.a, other drivers). Out of scope for now, not excluded: the long-term scope is the whole of IRIX and its add-ons.

Base user-space daemons and commands of the installed 6.5.30 system: hardware inventory and configuration, the controller and power-management tools, NFS, RPC and CacheFS services, the cluster daemons and the XFS repair tools. Listed so the inventory counts them; their functions are out of scope for now, not excluded.

selector_scope.reason: A syssgi selector is in scope when the first routine its code calls matches narrow_prefixes, the rule of the kernel image. first_call is a heuristic (blank when the code branches before calling anything), so a blank selector is out of scope for now, not excluded.
